hook: Spacewalks kept wearing astronauts out. This was the last chance.
narration: Spacewalks kept wearing astronauts out. This was Gemini's last chance to get one right.
November 1966. Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin launched on Gemini 12, the final Gemini flight.
Closing on their target rocket, the crew reported erratic radar readings.
So Aldrin bent over his charts and worked out the distances and burns by hand.
He had written his doctoral thesis on exactly this, rendezvous.
Lovell brought Gemini 12 right alongside the target.
Then came the spacewalk. Aldrin used handrails, foot restraints and a waist tether to stay in place.
In weightlessness, every push sends your body the other way. Earlier spacewalkers burned huge energy just holding still.
Doctors on the ground watched his heartbeat. It stayed mostly below one hundred twenty.
[short pause] He worked through nineteen tasks, then called his workstation clear.
outcome: Aldrin set a record of two hours and nine minutes of tethered spacewalk, and Gemini 12 splashed down beside the carrier Wasp.
title: Radar failed, so he did the math by hand
description:
In November 1966, on the last Gemini flight, the radar gave erratic readings during rendezvous and Buzz Aldrin worked the approach out from his charts. He then made a record two hour, nine minute tethered spacewalk, and Gemini 12 splashed down beside the USS Wasp. From the 1966 NASA film Gemini XII Mission.
